items.summary: GitLab has released critical patches for its Self-Hosted AI Gateway to address a vulnerability that could allow an authenticated user to escape the prompt template sandbox. GitLab strongly advises all self-managed customers to upgrade to the patched versions immediately.

items.title: FBI disrupts Chinese hacking tools used to breach critical infrastructure
items.one_liner: FBI domain seizures disrupt Flax Typhoon and Integrity Tech infrastructure used for global critical infrastructure scanning and intrusions.
items.summary: The FBI seized seven domains operated by China-based Integrity Technology Group on behalf of the Flax Typhoon hacking group, disrupting two platforms known as MicroScan and FishHub used to compromise critical infrastructure. MicroScan combined vulnerability scanning with Mirai botnets to target organizations including a South Carolina power company, Japanese and Polish airports, and Taiwanese energy and academic institutions. FishHub facilitated spear-phishing and malware delivery, granting unauthorized remote access and enabling data exfiltration across more than 20 organizations. United States authorities worked alongside international partners and domestic agencies to issue joint advisories and display seizure notices on the offending domains.
items.bottom_line: Seven domains supporting Chinese state-sponsored cyber operations against critical infrastructure have been seized by the FBI.

items.title: Attackers Hijack .gh, .sl, and .as Registries to Obtain Certificates for Google Domains
items.one_liner: Compromised .gh, .sl, and .as ccTLD registries allowed attackers to obtain and abuse HTTPS certificates for Google domains.
items.summary: Attackers compromised the country-code top-level domain registries for Ghana (.gh), Sierra Leone (.sl), and American Samoa (.as) by altering authoritative DNS records to obtain unauthorized HTTPS certificates. Certificate Transparency logs revealed at least 12 domain-validated certificates issued for Google and YouTube names between September 22 and 27 by Let's Encrypt and ZeroSSL. Although Google's internal systems were uncompromised, the certificates exposed encrypted traffic to potential interception. Google mitigated the incident by leveraging Chrome's CRLSets to block the certificates and coordinating rapid revocations with the issuing certificate authorities.
items.bottom_line: Attackers hijacked ccTLD DNS records to generate unauthorized HTTPS certificates for Google and other global brands, requiring emergency browser blocks and revocations.

items.title: Unpatched Critical LMCache Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code Remotely
items.one_liner: Ensure your LMCache multiprocess deployments are bound exclusively to localhost to prevent unauthenticated RCE.
items.summary: A critical remote code execution vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-105192 with a 9.8 CVSS severity score, affects LMCache versions 0.3.9 through 0.5.5 in multiprocess mode. The security flaw stems from an unauthenticated ZeroMQ socket that processes incoming Python pickle data without validation before checking message types. The vulnerability becomes remotely exploitable if administrators configure the standalone cache server to listen on a routable network address instead of localhost. Official container images run the vulnerable cache process with root privileges, and no patched release is currently available.
items.bottom_line: An unauthenticated RCE flaw in LMCache multiprocess mode allows remote code execution when bound to routable addresses.

items.title: Tensorlake npm Package Compromised to Deliver Shai-Hulud Credential-Stealing Worm
items.one_liner: The npm package tensorlake was compromised to distribute the Shai-Hulud credential-stealing worm and development environment persistence.
items.summary: The npm package 'tensorlake' was compromised in a supply chain attack involving malicious version 0.5.144, which delivers the Shai-Hulud credential-stealing worm. The payload utilizes an obfuscated loader and Bun runtime to harvest sensitive tokens, SSH keys, configuration files, and cloud credentials, while dropping the HackBrowserData binary. The worm establishes persistence, injects malicious VS Code and Claude configuration tasks to execute upon opening projects, and attempts exfiltration via custom endpoints or public GitHub repositories.
items.bottom_line: Version 0.5.144 of the tensorlake npm package contains a malicious worm that harvests cloud credentials, sets up persistence, and poisons local developer workspaces.

items.one_liner: Critical pre-auth arbitrary file read vulnerability (CVE-2026-21589) impacts Atlassian on-prem products.
items.summary: Atlassian published an out-of-band advisory for a critical pre-authentication arbitrary file read vulnerability (CVE-2026-21589) affecting multiple on-premise products including Bitbucket, Confluence, and Jira. Researchers analyzing the patches identified changes in the `atlassian-plugins-webresource` JAR files and noted WAF bypass complexities involving double colons and path traversal characters.

items.title: AI-powered fuzzing with the GitHub Security Lab Taskflow Agent
items.one_liner: GitHub's new autonomous fuzzing agent automates harness writing and crash triage for C/C++ repositories.
items.summary: The GitHub Security Lab has released the Fuzzing Taskflow, an autonomous fuzzing pipeline built on top of the Taskflow Agent framework designed for C and C++ projects. Developers can point the tool at any GitHub repository slug to automatically install software like AFL++, clone the repository, identify entry points, write fuzz harnesses, run campaigns, and triage crashes. The agent utilizes Claude Sonnet 5 by default to bypass frontier model guardrails and operates using shell drivers, taskflow YAMLs, and MCP tools. Because the agent executes build commands directly on the host without containerization, users are warned to run it exclusively within disposable environments.
items.bottom_line: Autonomous LLM fuzzing agents can manage the entire vulnerability discovery pipeline from harness generation to crash triage, but require isolated execution environments.

items.title: Alert: FortiBleed remains active campaign, can lock out users or lead to ransomware attacks
items.one_liner: The FortiBleed campaign continues to compromise hundreds of thousands of Fortinet firewalls and VPNs, locking out users and serving as an entry point for ransomware.
items.summary: The FortiBleed campaign continues to target internet-exposed Fortinet firewalls and VPN gateways using compromised credentials to lock out administrators and facilitate ransomware deployments. Originally uncovered with over 86,644 compromised devices, wider investigations indicate over 400,000 to 450,000 devices have been targeted in the broader operation. Attackers leverage unauthorized access to create new admin accounts and change passwords, rendering standard patching and password resets insufficient. Government agencies including the FBI and Secret Service warn that initial access brokers are supplying access to ransomware affiliates such as INC/Lynx and Payload, and recommend restricting external management and enforcing multifactor authentication.
key_facts: Initial discovery scale: 86,644 compromised devices across 194 countries
items.bottom_line: Fortinet devices exposed to the internet face active credential compromise and administrative lockout via FortiBleed, frequently preceding ransomware deployment.

items.title: Attackers Exploit AhsayCBS Flaws to Deploy XMRig Miners Disguised as Microsoft Edge
items.one_liner: Attackers are using AI-assisted scripts and kernel-level drivers to hide cryptominers on unpatched backup servers.
items.summary: Threat actors are exploiting two vulnerabilities in the AhsayCBS backup utility, CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134, to deploy XMRig miners and web shells. The attackers use an AI-assisted PowerShell script that monitors Windows Task Manager and terminates it to hide mining activity. The miners masquerade as "edge.exe" to avoid detection, and in some cases, the legitimate but vulnerable "WinRing0x64.sys" driver is used to gain kernel-level access. Although a patch was released (v10.3.4), researchers found it is still vulnerable, effectively making these zero-day threats.
items.bottom_line: AhsayCBS backup servers are under active attack by actors using AI-assisted evasion techniques; the current v10.3.4 patch is reportedly ineffective.

items.title: Anthropic Launches Free AI Vulnerability Scanner for Open-Source Projects
items.one_liner: Anthropic introduced a free, AI-driven vulnerability scanner for open-source projects using autonomous Claude models.
items.summary: Anthropic has launched OSS Scanner, an opt-in, automated AI vulnerability scanning service designed to secure open-source software projects using advanced models like Claude Mythos. Core maintainers can enroll by submitting a pull request containing a repository configuration and a Dockerfile, allowing autonomous agents to execute audits without internet access. The tool has already identified over 29,000 candidate vulnerabilities and generated 584 advisories across major projects. Anthropic does not enforce a rigid 90-day disclosure period initially due to potential false positives, but will coordinate human-validated disclosures through its existing CVD policy.
items.bottom_line: Open-source maintainers can now leverage automated AI agents for zero-cost, periodic security audits through Anthropic's OSS Scanner.

items.summary: Japan's National Police Agency has confirmed the arrest and extradition of a 28-year-old Russian national linked to the Qilin ransomware gang. items.summary: CISA has added a path traversal vulnerability in ONLYONLYOFFICE Docs Server, tracked as CVE-2021-3199, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. items.title: Windows Exploitation Techniques: Dangling COM Object Registrations
items.one_liner: Dangling COM registrations in Windows allow for privilege escalation via malicious DLL injection.
items.summary: Researchers have detailed a privilege escalation technique targeting a dangling COM object registration in Windows, identified as CVE-2026-66804. The vulnerability stems from a missing server executable for the CrossDevice COM object, allowing an attacker to place a malicious DLL in a user-writable directory to achieve code execution in privileged processes. This serves as an alternative exploit path following the incomplete fix for the 'Dark Elevator' bug (CVE-2026-50343). The researchers demonstrate that custom COM marshaling can be used to force the loading of the malicious DLL into a privileged service.
items.bottom_line: Attackers can achieve privilege escalation by placing a malicious DLL in a predictable path to exploit a dangling COM object registration.

items.title: Researchers Publish Working Exploit for Pre-Auth AnyDesk Linux Flaw That Gives Root Access
items.one_liner: A public exploit for a pre-auth root RCE in AnyDesk Linux (AnyPwn) highlights the risks of unpatched legacy builds and silent vendor fixes.
items.summary: Security researchers have released a working exploit, dubbed AnyPwn, for a pre-authentication remote code execution vulnerability in AnyDesk Linux. The flaw is a heap buffer overflow in the session protocol that allows attackers to gain root access via direct TCP connections on port 7070. Although AnyDesk patched the issue in version 8.0.3 in June, they did not assign a CVE or issue a formal security advisory, leading to confusion regarding the vulnerability's scope. Administrators are advised to update to the latest version or restrict access to the affected port.
items.bottom_line: AnyDesk Linux users must update to version 8.0.3 or higher and restrict access to port 7070 to prevent root-level exploitation via the AnyPwn exploit.

items.title: Flax Typhoon Exploits Five Flaws as CISA Sets October 11 Deadline for Federal Agencies
items.one_liner: A new CISA mandate requires patching five critical vulnerabilities exploited by Flax Typhoon, including RCEs in ProFTPD and Apache Struts, by October 11, 2026.
items.summary: CISA has added five vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog following their active abuse by the China-linked threat actor Flax Typhoon. These flaws, which include remote code execution and command injection vulnerabilities in software like ProFTPD, ONLYOFFICE, and Apache Struts, are being used to gain initial access and siphon sensitive data. Federal agencies are mandated to patch these vulnerabilities or discontinue the affected software by October 11, 2026. The activity is part of a broader campaign involving scanning tools and password spraying, often targeting Microsoft Exchange servers.

items.bottom_line: Federal agencies must remediate these five specific vulnerabilities by October 11, 2026, to mitigate active exploitation by Flax Typhoon.

items.summary: Threat actors are increasingly adopting Web3 and blockchain-based smart contracts for command-and-control (C2) infrastructure to bypass static detection. Security teams are advised to monitor for blockchain-related network traffic and automate policy controls across CI/CD runners to mitigate these risks.

items.title: OAuth grants pile up faster than you can review them. Here's how to keep up.
items.one_liner: Overprivileged and unmanaged OAuth grants create hidden enterprise attack paths that defy manual review and require agentic automation.
items.summary: Enterprise environments face severe governance challenges due to the accumulation of unmanaged OAuth grants, which operate outside of traditional SSO and MFA controls and can outlive employee credentials. A single compromised token from a third-party tool like Context.ai was previously shown to cause significant breaches, such as the Vercel security incident. On average, employees create 88 OAuth grants each, with 31 possessing data-level permissions, rendering manual vetting by security teams completely unsustainable. Gartner predicts that half of all SaaS breaches will stem from overprivileged OAuth tokens by 2027, making agentic capabilities critical for automated risk management.
key_facts: Gartner prediction: 50% of SaaS breaches from overprivileged OAuth tokens by 2027
items.bottom_line: Traditional identity controls fail to govern OAuth tokens, meaning organizations must deploy automated or agentic tools to prevent widespread SaaS breaches.

This flaw occurs due to missing authentication and nonce checks on the wp_loaded handler, coupled with unescaped echo into a Dompdf-rendered HTML template with PHP execution enabled. Unauthenticated attackers can exploit this via a single POST request to execute code on the server. Site administrators must update the plugin immediately to secure their WordPress installations.
key_facts: Affected Plugin: 3D Product configurator for WooCommerce <= 2.16.2
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can achieve remote code execution on WordPress sites running vulnerable versions of the 3D Product configurator plugin via a single POST request.

items.title: CVE-2026-108263 - Astron Agent: Unsandboxed code-node leads to cross-tenant RCE
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-108263 in Astron Agent lets low-privilege tenants achieve cross-tenant RCE due to an unsandboxed local code executor.
items.summary: A critical cross-tenant Remote Code Execution vulnerability, designated CVE-2026-108263, affects the Astron Agent AI workflow platform prior to version 1.1.2. The vulnerability exists because the default workflow code-node path defaults to `LocalExecutor` when `CODE_EXEC_TYPE` is unset, executing dynamic code without documented sandbox restrictions and providing complete Python builtins. The issue has been patched in version 1.1.2.
items.bottom_line: Astron Agent before 1.1.2 contains an unsandboxed code-node vulnerability allowing authenticated low-privilege tenants to achieve root RCE and cross-tenant data access.

items.title: CVE-2026-103413: Apache Camel Karavan: unvalidated Kubernetes resources applied from a project's kubernetes.yaml
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-103413 in Apache Camel Karavan allows authenticated users to apply unvalidated Kubernetes resources and execute privileged deployments.
items.summary: A high-severity input validation vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-103413 with a CVSS score of 8.8, has been disclosed in Apache Camel Karavan versions 4.0.0 before 4.22.1. When starting a deployment, Karavan unmarshalled a project's `kubernetes.yaml` file and applied all contained resources directly to the cluster without validating resource kinds, rejecting security-sensitive pod options, or pinning the namespace. This allowed any authenticated user to deploy arbitrary Kubernetes resources within the reach of its service account, including privileged containers, host network access, and host path volumes. The issue was resolved in version 4.22.1 by the Apache Camel team.
items.bottom_line: Apache Camel Karavan versions 4.0.0 to 4.22.0 contain an 8.8-severity vulnerability allowing arbitrary Kubernetes resource deployment from project configuration files.

items.one_liner: If you use Apache CXF with the Netty transport, you are vulnerable to MitM attacks due to missing hostname verification.
items.summary: Apache CXF's Netty-based HTTP client transport suffered from a vulnerability where it failed to verify that the hostname in a server's TLS certificate matched the target host. The flaw affected Apache CXF versions 4.2.0 before 4.2.4, 4.0.0 before 4.1.9, and versions prior to 3.6.13. Users can resolve the issue by upgrading to fixed versions 4.2.4, 4.1.9, or 3.6.13.

items.summary: A vulnerability in Apache CXF (CVE-2026-97791) allows the STSTokenValidator to accept untrusted SAML assertions because validation state is improperly shared across multiple requests in a single object. items.title: [0day-rubbish] Advantech WebAccess Node 9.2.3 unauthenticated CrystalRpt.aspx file upload and path traversal to code execution in w3wp.exe (9.8)
items.one_liner: A critical 9.8 CVSS unauthenticated file upload and path traversal vulnerability in Advantech WebAccess Node allows remote code execution.
items.summary: The 0day Rubbish Research Team disclosed a critical unauthenticated vulnerability in Advantech WebAccess Node 9.2.3, a closed-source industrial SCADA/HMI web server. Tracked with a CVSS score of 9.8, the flaw combines unrestricted file upload (CWE-434), path traversal (CWE-22), and missing authorization (CWE-306) within the CrystalRpt.aspx form handler. An attacker can supply a crafted nodeName parameter with double dot-traversal sequences (	extbackslash..	extbackslash..) to bypass validation checks and write an arbitrary ASP.NET file to the application root directory. Subsequent requests to the uploaded file cause the build manager to compile and execute it within w3wp.exe under high privileges, achieving unauthenticated remote code execution. Mitigation requires proper extension validation and reordering file processing checks before saving files to disk.
key_facts: Vulnerability Types: Unrestricted File Upload (CWE-434), Path Traversal (CWE-22), Missing Authorization (CWE-306)
items.bottom_line: Advantech WebAccess Node 9.2.3 contains an unauthenticated RCE vulnerability via path traversal and unrestricted file upload, demanding immediate patching.

claims.text: The chain is three HTTP requests plus a follow-on GET, leading to execution inside w3wp.exe running cmd.exe /c.
claims.support_span: The chain is three HTTP requests plus a follow-on GET. Request 1 harvests __VIEWSTATE (1056 bytes) and __EVENTVALIDATION (92 bytes) while establishing the traversed destination. Request 3 GETs the written page, which the build manager compiles on first request and executes inside w3wp.exe, running cmd.exe /c with captured stdout.

items.title: How I Found a $113,337 AF_ALG Linux Local Privilege Escalation Before Copy Fail
items.one_liner: CVE-2025-39964 is a Linux kernel AF_ALG race condition that grants root privilege escalation and container escape.
items.summary: Researchers detailed the discovery of CVE-2025-39964, a race condition vulnerability in the Linux kernel's AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem. The flaw allows an unprivileged user to execute out-of-bounds access, escalate privileges to root, and escape Docker containers. Discovered by Muhammad Alifa Ramdhan and completed with Billy Jheng Bing-Jhong at STAR Labs, the bug earned a $113,337 reward through Google's kernelCTF program. Unlike Copy Fail, which is a straight-line logic flaw in the AEAD path, CVE-2025-39964 involves a race between writers sharing an AF_ALG socket present since 2011.
key_facts: Affected Subsystem: Linux kernel AF_ALG API
items.bottom_line: Unprivileged users can abuse cryptographic API race conditions in the Linux kernel to achieve root privilege escalation and container escapes.

items.title: A Single POST Freezes Any Next.js Server https://simonkoeck.com/writeups/react-rsc-formdata-event-loop-dos @secharvester
items.one_liner: A single malicious POST request containing nested form pointers can saturate the Node.js event loop and freeze any Next.js server via React server actions.
items.summary: A denial-of-service vulnerability in React's server action form data reconstruction logic allows a single crafted HTTP POST request to freeze any Next.js server. When processing server actions, React parses nested form pointers designated by the '$K' prefix by iteratively scanning the entire list of request fields for each pointer without rate-limiting or yielding. An attacker can supply 10,000 pointers and 10,000 fields—buried one level deep to bypass array-nesting and argument-count limits—triggering roughly 100 million unpaused string checks that completely saturate Node.js's single-threaded event loop. Because this payload parsing occurs prior to authentication checks or session validation, public endpoints or any valid user account can freeze the server for several seconds per request.
key_facts: Impact: Server freeze for ~4 seconds per request on test hardware
items.bottom_line: Next.js applications handling React server actions are vulnerable to pre-authentication denial of service via algorithmic complexity attacks on form data parsing.

claims.text: Put 10,000 pointers and 10,000 fields in one request, and React makes 10,000 passes over 10,000 fields.

items.summary: The BPFDoor Linux backdoor remains a critical threat to network edge devices, operating silently by waiting for a specific "magic packet" rather than beaconing or opening conventional listening ports. According to Rapid7 Intelligence VP Christiaan Beek, threat actors actively target network edge infrastructure such as mail security gateways, VPN appliances, and firewalls because these vendor-managed appliances are internet-exposed, trusted, and incapable of running standard endpoint detection and response (EDR) agents. Compromising these devices allows adversaries to blend malicious traffic into normal operations and establish long-term persistence. In telecom environments, such persistent edge access can compromise core signaling flows, subscriber identifiers, and lawful intercept capabilities, posing severe national security implications.
key_facts: Target devices: Mail security gateways, VPN appliances, firewalls
items.bottom_line: Targeting network edge appliances with silent backdoors like BPFDoor allows attackers to establish persistent, undetected footholds that compromise critical enterprise and telecom infrastructure.

items.title: Building Reliable Data Analytics Agents: Lessons from the KDD Cup
items.one_liner: NVIDIA's KGMON team secured second in the KDD Cup data agents competition by optimizing the agent harness around a unified SQL interface.
items.summary: The NVIDIA KGMON team secured second place in the KDD Cup 2026 Data Agents competition by focusing on building a smaller, more verifiable agent harness rather than an open-ended model structure. Tasked with answering natural-language queries across heterogeneous data sources like SQL databases, CSVs, JSONs, documents, and videos using a fixed small LLM, the team constrained the action space and normalized access. They converted file-based data into a unified SQLite database and implemented custom Python functions alongside a read-only schema-scouting step. This architectural approach reduced routing errors and enhanced reasoning reliability for small open models.
items.bottom_line: Constraining action space and normalizing data into a unified SQL interface significantly improves the reliability of data analytics agents powered by small LLMs.

items.one_liner: Malware authors are embedding natural-language instructions to trick automated AI analysis pipelines into false verdicts.
items.summary: Cisco Talos has classified an archetype of malware named 'A3: AI-Analysis Evasion,' where malware embeds natural-language instructions designed to obstruct or manipulate automated LLM analysis pipelines. Defenders must ensure analysis pipelines treat sample content strictly as evidence rather than executable instructions.

items.bottom_line: AI analysis tools must be architected to isolate file contents as data rather than instructions to prevent evasion.

items.one_liner: Huntress details forensic recovery methods for mapping Akira ransomware movements when EDR telemetry is installed post-compromise.
items.summary: Huntress researchers pieced together a post-compromise Akira ransomware attack on a domain controller using Windows Registry artifacts, event logs, and Akira log files. The investigation highlights how limited EDR telemetry can be supplemented by multi-artifact endpoint forensics to map threat actor progression.

items.title: Why the AI Attack Surface Extends Your Stack
items.one_liner: Enterprise AI integrations expand the attack surface beyond models to surrounding tools, APIs, and cloud infrastructure, enabling complex multi-layer attack chains.
items.summary: Integrating Large Language Models into enterprise workflows significantly expands the traditional application security attack surface beyond the model itself. Because LLMs can autonomously invoke tools, retrieve data across APIs, and act as intelligence layers, prompt injections and security flaws can trigger cascading failures across the entire software stack. Conventional security scans and model safety checks often miss these complex attack chains, which can lead to remote code execution, credential theft, and cross-tenant data exposure when service accounts possess overly broad permissions. Security leaders must map what AI systems can access and execute realistic attack scenarios across all underlying infrastructure layers.
items.bottom_line: Enterprise AI security requires mapping full stack integrations and testing realistic attack chains rather than relying solely on traditional perimeter defenses or model safety scans.

items.summary: Gilnett's wstrace is a high-performance, standalone Windows system and API monitor written in Rust that operates completely in userland without requiring kernel drivers. It serves as a modern alternative to strace and Process Monitor, utilizing Win32 APIs and Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) to capture telemetry within process security boundaries. Engineered for high-security enterprise environments, wstrace is 100% offline, initiates zero remote telemetry, and retains all captured API logs locally in RAM. It supports multiple deployment mechanisms including PowerShell installation, winget, and scoop, targeting both x86_64 and ARM64 Windows architectures.
items.bottom_line: wstrace provides kernel-driverless Windows process tracing in Rust, ensuring full data sovereignty with zero outbound network calls.

items.title: [tl;dr sec] #348 - Google's PageBreak Scanner, Perplexity's Agent Security Tool, Defending Agentically
items.one_liner: Google's PageBreak agentic security scanner uses deterministic validation with Gemini models to root out hundreds of web vulnerabilities with minimal false positives.
items.summary: Google's Product Security team has developed PageBreak, an agentic security scanner utilizing Gemini 3.1 Pro and 3.5 Flash that has discovered over 500 XSS bugs in Google web applications since November 2025. PageBreak achieves near-zero false positives by enforcing deterministic validation where every hypothesis triggers real payloads, such as executing JavaScript for XSS, writing world-readable files for path traversal, or causing outbound DNS queries for RCE. Additionally, the scan tested a high-assurance web framework designed to eliminate whole classes of web bugs by default.

items.bottom_line: Deterministic validation is the key to making LLM-driven security agents practical for finding high-confidence web vulnerabilities at scale.

items.summary: The speed gap in cybersecurity: Navigating the shift from human speed to machine-driven attacks The most consequential effect of artificial intelligence on cybersecurity may not be that it invents entirely new categories of attack. It may be that it changes the economics of attacks we already know. Phishing, credential theft, ransomware, exploitation of software vulnerabilities and social engineering are not new. What is changing is how cheaply, quickly and repeatedly an adversary can execute them. When technology lowers the cost of reconnaissance, content generation, vulnerability discovery and attack scaling at the same time, the result is not just more cybercrime.

items.summary: The Kerala High Court ordered the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau to register an FIR against former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter T. Veena, and son-in-law P.A. Legal experts note that the order bypassed statutory safeguards under Section 17(A) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, which mandates prior approval before investigating public servants, and denied the accused an opportunity to be heard. The Enforcement Directorate intends to utilize the resulting FIR as a predicate offense for money laundering investigations under the PMLA, though the act does not directly apply to Ms. Veena as a non-public servant.

items.one_liner: HiPHI provides a large-scale motion capture dataset for training physical humanoid robot manipulation policies.
items.summary: IEEE Spectrum highlights HiPHI, a large-scale motion capture dataset designed to bridge the training data gap for humanoid robotics.
